brief: Societe Generale's base case is that elevated single-stock volatility and low index correlation persist, a divergence last seen in the dot-com era, because AI capex is distorting the classic volatility cycle. Corporate profit margins are near 75-year highs, leverage is low and credit spreads are benign, supporting the profit cycle and limiting near-term equity tail risk. Two risks flow from the AI capex boom: rising debt financing raises sensitivity to long-term rates, and hyperscaler and semiconductor credit default swap spreads have widened above the US investment-grade index, implying over 10% five-year default probability at 40% recovery. SG estimates correlation fair value is 5-10 points above current levels, allowing index volatility to rise 4-5 vol points, but sees no sharp spike without a growth scare, keeping dispersion trades favorable, especially in the US where realised dispersion still exceeds implied. Energy is flagged as the best sector hedge because it is negatively correlated with the rest of the market. Equity funding costs spiked to 101bp on the S&P 500 3-month cost of funding in June on leveraged-ETF and hedge-fund semiconductor demand, then partially normalized, though long-dated costs stay elevated and have reversed their old inverse link to spot, now rising alongside rallies.
